technicalcautions.claim_location: Opening thesis; latency budget table; transport comparison
technicalcautions.correction: WebRTC is a strong fit, not the sole possible voice transport. UDP media avoids TCP stream head-of-line delay but WebRTC can use TCP/TLS relays. Fixed transport/model latency ranges and a universal conversational threshold are not guarantees.
technicalcautions.status: conceptual correction; numeric claims not independently qualified

technicalcautions.claim_location: SFU scaling section and multi-region Redis/media-relay explanation
technicalcautions.correction: Do not generalize the described cross-SFU room mesh to self-hosted LiveKit. Official self-hosted distributed documentation says one room fits on one node; Redis coordinates routing/signaling. Mesh/MCU/SFU participant cutoffs are workload-dependent, not architectural hard limits.

technicalcautions.claim_location: Room metadata; participant kind; cheap rooms; related agent/service claims
technicalcautions.correction: Room metadata is an opaque string; attributes are key/value pairs. Participant kind does not bypass grants. Common media primitives coexist with separate AgentServer, SIP, ingress and egress lifecycles. Room creation and forwarding still have resource limits.

technicalcautions.claim_location: Reliability/ordering; transactional RPC; room metadata
technicalcautions.correction: Reliable live delivery is not durable storage, replay or an atomic business transaction. Preserve operation identities and explicit acceptance when an RPC response is lost. Stream ordering has a defined stream/transport scope; metadata is not a database.

technicalcautions.claim_location: E2EE key negotiation/rotation and encrypted application scope
technicalcautions.correction: Application code must securely generate and distribute keys. An authorized agent can decrypt content it processes; a plaintext-consuming provider remains part of the trust path. Distinguish transport encryption from configured E2EE and from signaling/API visibility.

technicalcautions.claim_location: Server and agent SDK parity tables; competitive breadth claims
technicalcautions.correction: Shared abstractions do not promise identical plugins, APIs or features across languages and releases. Check the selected SDK/plugin release and platform; a catalogue or marketing breadth claim is not compatibility evidence.

proposed_questions.title: A conversational task is not a durable workflow
proposed_questions.question: When would you use AgentTask, the conversational TaskGroup, asyncio.TaskGroup, or P1 accepted work?
proposed_questions.answer: Use AgentTask for a focused multi-turn exchange that temporarily controls the current session and returns a value. In pinned 1.8.11 await the task instance; complete(result) settles its future, but a generic result annotation does not validate the value. Validate collected data explicitly. The beta conversational TaskGroup sequences factories identified by stable IDs and returns keyed results; revisiting a step changes conversational collection, not an external receipt. asyncio.TaskGroup instead owns related Python tasks and their failures within a process. P1 provides the persisted acceptance, issuance, receipts and recovery contract when business work must outlive that process.

followups.question: If a user corrects an earlier address, what is rolled back?
followups.answer: The conversational group can collect the address again and replace its derived result. Any already committed external operation keeps its original identity and receipt; a new change needs the domain’s own revision and authorization contract.

followups.question: Does AgentTask[Address] ensure complete(value) contains an Address?
followups.answer: No. In this pin complete stores the supplied value or exception. Construct and validate a runtime model or validate at the consuming boundary; type hints guide tools and static analysis rather than proving domain validity.

proposed_questions.title: Keep context useful without promoting it to authority
proposed_questions.question: How would you preserve a returning caller’s context while keeping userdata, chat history and durable state distinct?
proposed_questions.answer: Construct userdata explicitly from trusted, scoped reads; room or token metadata does not automatically hydrate AgentSession. Keep it as a convenient session object, not the source of consent or recovery. ChatContext contains messages, function calls, outputs and transition/configuration items. Trimming a messages-only list can orphan tool relationships or lose important context. Use the selected SDK’s context operations and retain the domain facts needed for current reasoning. For this POC, P2 rehydration loads authorized observations with separate as-of boundaries; P1 remains the business authority. Summaries and retrieved text help the model answer but cannot approve a mutation.

followups.question: Why is persisting only on_exit insufficient?
followups.answer: A normal handoff may run the hook, but abrupt process loss may prevent it. Persist accepted business facts at their own authority boundary. Treat conversational state snapshots as recoverable convenience with an explicit replay/hydration policy.

followups.question: May old tool output be summarized into a system instruction?
followups.answer: A summary remains a derived observation. Preserve provenance, scope and any freshness limits, and frame retrieved content as data. A system-message role alone must not grant the summarized material authority over domain guards.

proposed_questions.title: Name the signal that ends the turn
proposed_questions.question: Explain how VAD, streaming STT, text end-of-turn detection and realtime provider turn control differ.
proposed_questions.answer: VAD estimates whether the audio contains speech. Streaming STT produces provisional/final text while audio is arriving. The text MultilingualModel uses STT conversation context and STT-reported language to estimate whether a turn is complete; it is not the adaptive audio-interruption classifier. Endpointing applies a mode-specific wait policy, so do not blindly add every configured silence delay. A realtime provider can own turn control instead, or a supported integration can supply separate STT and choose the framework detector. Select one controlling path. The POC’s manual P2 path additionally requires durable intake before its dispatched generation; recognizing a final transcript alone does not satisfy that invariant.

followups.question: What changed in newer official turn-detector guidance?
followups.answer: Current documentation also describes an audio detector and deprecates the text detector for a future major version. State the chosen plugin and release; do not attribute the audio model’s inputs or timing behavior to the text MultilingualModel.

followups.question: Does max endpointing delay cap all response latency?
followups.answer: No. It controls a turn-ending policy in its selected mode. Transcript availability, model calls, tools, synthesis, transport and playout have other timing boundaries and need their own budgets and observations.

proposed_questions.title: Separate interruption onset from recovery
proposed_questions.question: An agent stops speaking on background noise and later resumes. Which controls would you inspect, and what must business work do?
proposed_questions.answer: Inspect the actual turn/interruption mode, VAD quality, onset minimum duration/word thresholds and adaptive detector observations. false_interruption_timeout is not a delay before stopping speech: it governs silence after an interruption, when the framework can identify a false interruption and resume without user transcription. In this pin the activity can pause output before this recovery decision. A short stop can be a real command, while a longer acknowledgment can still be feedback, so use labeled representative audio. Preserve the accepted P1/P2 operation and output observations. Interruption stops or pauses conversation output; business cancellation requires its own explicit policy and cannot erase a possible external effect.

followups.question: Should increasing the recovery timeout prevent the initial cutoff?
followups.answer: No. It changes how long recovery waits after the interruption. To address onset false positives, inspect the selected audio signal and onset/adaptive controls, then measure cutoff and resume behavior separately.

followups.question: How would you evaluate the setting?
followups.answer: Label intended stops, backchannels, noise and silence across languages and environments. Measure false interruption, missed interruption, output stop/resume latency and user task outcomes; word count alone is not ground truth.

proposed_questions.title: Respect the extension point contract
proposed_questions.question: You want RAG before generation and pronunciation fixes before synthesis. Which extension points would you use and what must their code preserve?
proposed_questions.answer: Use on_user_turn_completed(self, turn_ctx, new_message) for bounded pre-generation enrichment. Its default body is pass; returning normally continues, while StopResponse explicitly stops automatic reply generation. Keep retrieved text scoped, bounded and untrusted. For pronunciation, transform the asynchronous text stream in tts_node and forward ModelSettings to the default node, yielding AudioFrames. Other nodes have their own audio, context, tool and chunk contracts. Preserve cancellation and close any independently created resource; lazy iteration alone does not guarantee that. In the P2 manual adapter, this hook must also preserve the existing durable-admission order rather than create a competing intake path.

followups.question: Can you skip a default hook call to suppress the reply?

proposed_questions.title: Approve streamed output before it escapes
proposed_questions.question: How would you review a node that streams JSON response text to TTS while filtering disallowed content?
proposed_questions.answer: Trace every yield and every buffer. If original chunks escape before a sentence is approved, a later replacement cannot retract spoken content. Bound retained bytes/time, handle malformed/incomplete structures explicitly, and validate the intended schema and domain values rather than merely parsing JSON. Respect the actual ChatChunk structure, including tool calls and other required metadata. Bind emotion or rendering metadata to the response that produced it rather than a mutable shared last value. Choose the latency cost of withholding output deliberately, test chunk-split forbidden patterns and failure paths, and keep sensitive generated reasoning out of logs. Display-only filtering is a separate boundary from audio release.

followups.question: Is fail-open always wrong on moderation failure?
followups.answer: The policy depends on the product, but it must be explicit and truthful. A parse failure is unknown, not a positive safe verdict. Decide whether to withhold, use a constrained fallback or escalate; test that branch independently.

followups.question: Can text filtering protect a realtime model from original audio?
followups.answer: Not if that audio has already been sent to the provider. Apply the required protection before that ingress boundary or select another architecture. Similarly, filtering a transcript after synthesis cannot retract published speech.

proposed_questions.title: Configure the hybrid you actually intend
proposed_questions.question: How would you combine realtime audio understanding with controlled speech output, and prove a handoff really changed model paths?
proposed_questions.answer: For a supported turn-based realtime model, configure text-only output and a separate TTS to control voice and scripted wording. Confirm the exact provider/plugin supports that modality; current full-duplex behavior is a distinct contract. A parallel STT observer can supply timely text when needed, but must not create competing turn authority. For a realtime-to-cascade handoff, configure the target agent’s STT, text LLM, TTS and turn policy explicitly. In this SDK unspecified models inherit from the session, so changing persona alone does not change the pipeline. Measure the resulting output path and own both providers’ lifetimes; do not infer health from successful client construction.

followups.question: Would separate TTS guarantee lower latency?
followups.answer: No. It adds another configured component and changes streaming, buffering, cost and output control. Compare the same workload and audible timing boundaries; provider load, utterance length and turn policy can dominate the result.

followups.question: How should fallback interact with durable work?
followups.answer: Use an explicit permitted model/provider transition and preserve the original accepted operation and receipts. Retrying conversation generation is not permission to repeat an uncertain business effect. Qualification must observe actual new-path output, not only a selected-mode badge.

proposed_questions.title: Test conversation quality without weakening correctness
proposed_questions.question: What belongs in deterministic SDK tests, model-behavior evaluations and real audio experiments?
proposed_questions.answer: Use deterministic tests for runtime schemas, tool/domain authorization, exact operation identities, output gating and resource ownership. Use AgentSession.run with explicit event assertions to check tool names, arguments, outputs and handoffs; model-generated wording or a semantic judge adds stochastic behavior and may call a provider. Keep credentials and costs in an explicit test lane. Real audio is still needed for recognition, turn-taking, noise, interruption and playout claims. Compare labeled representative cases with defined latency boundaries, failures, versions and sample sizes. A mock using invented event fields can pass while the installed integration fails, and an illustrative benchmark table is not evidence for this application.

followups.question: What if a semantic judge is flaky?
followups.answer: Inspect failed transcripts and the intended behavior first. Calibrate the rubric against human labels and repeat a declared evaluation set. Keep hard business invariants deterministic; do not broaden the rubric merely to turn unexplained failures green.

followups.question: Which latency number would you publish?
followups.answer: Name the start and finish precisely, such as observed user speech end to first rendered agent audio, and disclose measurement limitations. Report distribution, failures, sample count, region and version; keep model TTFB and hook duration as separate supporting metrics.
